title: The Second Garden
premise: Mara Villalobos, a widowed father running the town's only bookshop, has spent seven years keeping love safely in the past tense. When a legal error places his late wife's estranged sister, Ines, as co-owner of the stubborn orchard threatening to swallow his shop's future, the two are forced into a reluctant partnership neither wants. As the harvest festival deadline looms and a developer's offer tempts Mara with the money that could secure his daughter's future, he uncovers that Ines signed away her inheritance years ago to protect him from a truth about his wife. In the end, Mara chooses truth over the career-saving deal, and he and Ines plant a new orchard together on ground finally cleared of secrets.
about_author: U. M. Oyelaran is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes love stories rooted in land, grief, and second chances. Their work has appeared in several literary journals, though The Second Garden is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A surveyor arrives at the bookshop with an orchard deed listing two names: Mara's and one he hasn't spoken in a decade—Ines. Emotional beat: quiet dread as the careful walls of his invisible life begin to crack.

chapters.title: Ines Comes Home
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She returns to town for the funeral of the orchard's old caretaker, expecting nothing, and finds her name entangled with a brother-in-law who won't meet her eyes. Emotional beat: guarded resentment masking old guilt.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced by a lawyer to jointly decide the orchard's fate before the festival, Mara and Ines negotiate an uneasy truce over bad coffee. Emotional beat: friction softening into wary curiosity.

chapters.title: What Lucia Left in the Soil
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Working the neglected trees, Ines finds letters Lucia buried in a tin box—letters that hint at a sacrifice Ines made long ago. Emotional beat: nostalgia curdling into fear of exposure.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A development company offers Mara enough money to pay off the bookshop's debts and fund his daughter's education—if he can deliver sole ownership. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as responsibility.

chapters.title: Festival Lights, Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the town's lantern festival, Mara and Ines share a dance that neither can call accidental, witnessed by neighbors whose gossip threatens both their reputations. Emotional beat: desire breaking through denial.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Digging through county records to force Ines out, Mara discovers her signature on an old waiver—and realizes she gave up her inheritance years ago, deliberately. Emotional beat: suspicion transformed into vertigo.

chapters.title: Truth in the Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Confronted, Ines confesses: Lucia was dying when she asked Ines to sign away the orchard so Mara would never learn how much Lucia had hidden from him. Emotional beat: betrayal and compassion colliding.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the developer's deadline at dawn, Mara must choose between signing away the orchard—the career that saved everything—or tearing up the contract and trusting Ines. Emotional beat: the loneliest hour before commitment.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara rejects the deal, publicly claims the truth about Lucia, and asks Ines to stay—not as co-owner by accident but by choice. They graft new saplings onto the old roots as the festival ends. Emotional beat: love chosen in full light, grief finally given somewhere to grow.
